title: Hypervisor Architecture and the Trust Boundary
description: Two side-by-side stacks contrast a Type 1 bare-metal hypervisor with a Type 2 hosted hypervisor, showing where the trust boundary sits, the VM-escape threat, and why the added host OS layer enlarges the attack surface.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

educational.topic: System Security: OS, Memory, and Access Control
learningObjectives: Distinguish Type 1 (bare-metal) from Type 2 (hosted) hypervisor architectures.
Identify the VM-escape threat that crosses the hypervisor trust boundary.
Explain why the Type 2 host OS layer creates a larger attack surface.
educational.prerequisites: Basic understanding of operating systems and virtual machines.

pedagogical.interaction: Two static SVG stacks with hover/tap band tooltips; reflows to a single column on narrow screens.
pedagogical.assessment: Lesson plan asks students to compare trust boundaries and explain why cloud uses Type 1.
pedagogical.misconceptions: Counters the idea that the two hypervisor types have the same attack surface.

chapter_title: "System Security: OS, Memory, and Access Control"
